This article compares regional compliance with Indikator 3, a quality metric tracking the proportion of ADHD assessment processes that include a diagnostic conference with a child and adolescent psychiatry specialist no later than 120 days after the assessment begins. The established standard for this indicator requires a 90% compliance rate.

Across all measured periods, no region in Denmark meets the ≥90% target. For the 2022/23 reporting year, Nordjylland (North Jutland) was the highest-performing region at 34%, while Syddanmark (Southern Denmark) recorded the lowest compliance at 10% [^src1]. The national average (Danmark) stood at 21%, with Hovedstaden (Capital Region) at 23%, Sjælland (Zealand) at 31%, and Midtjylland (Central Jutland) at 19% [^src1]. 

Data for the subsequent period from 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2024 shows a uniform 0% compliance rate across all regions, which likely indicates incomplete data registration for the ongoing year rather than an actual drop to zero [^src1]. In the earlier 2021/22 period, the table reports raw counts instead of percentages; for example, Sjælland documented 208 compliant cases out of 495 total assessments, while Midtjylland reported 181 out of 1,356 [^src1]. Ultimately, the data illustrates a systemic failure to meet the 120-day diagnostic conference requirement across all Danish regions.

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner regional opfyldelse af Indikator 3 for 2023/24 og tidligere år, og viser at ingen region opfylder standarden på ≥90 %, med laveste værdier i Danmark (0 %) og Syddanmark (10 %), og højeste i Nordjylland (34 %).
